concepts.def: Energy production using oxygen, dominant in long-duration, lower-intensity exercise and producing the most ATP.
An anaerobic system providing rapid energy for about 10 seconds of all-out effort, using phosphocreatine.
An anaerobic system breaking down glucose without oxygen for high-intensity work lasting up to a few minutes, producing lactate.
The maximum rate at which the body can take in and use oxygen, a key measure of aerobic fitness.
Changes such as increased heart rate, stroke volume and cardiac output that deliver more oxygen during exercise.
Excess post-exercise oxygen consumption: the extra oxygen used after exercise to restore the body to its resting state.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Physiological Factors Affecting Performance — a core area of A-Level PE.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Physiological Factors Affecting Performance brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Physiological Factors Affecting Performance.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which energy system dominates during a 100-metre sprint lasting about 10 seconds?
options: The ATP-PC system
The aerobic system
The glycolytic system mainly
No energy system
The maximum rate of oxygen uptake and use
Maximum heart rate only
Lung volume at rest
Body mass

mcqs.q: During exercise, cardiac output increases mainly because of a rise in:
options: Heart rate and stroke volume
Body temperature only
Bone density
Reaction time

mcqs.q: The aerobic system is the main energy source during:
options: A long-distance run
A single maximal jump
A 5-second sprint
A standing rest with no movement change

mcqs.q: Which energy system fuels a 10-second maximal sprint?
options: The ATP-PC system
The aerobic system
Resting lung volume
The glycolytic system mainly
Maximum heart rate only
By reducing stroke volume
Resting lung volume
The maximum rate of oxygen uptake and use

mcqs.q: How does the body increase cardiac output during exercise?
options: By reducing stroke volume
By lowering heart rate
By raising heart rate and stroke volume
Resting lung volume
